description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing a cavitary lesion in the right upper lung.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph demonstrating a cavitary lesion in the right upper lung field, as indicated by an arrow. The lesion appears as a radiolucent area with a surrounding zone of increased opacity. The mediastinum and cardiac silhouette are within normal limits. There are no visible pleural effusions. Electrodes and a line are visible, likely related to monitoring or medical devices.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the right upper lung

description.short_caption: Chest CT scan showing bilateral cavitary lesions in the lungs.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates bilateral cavitary lesions in the upper lobes of the lungs. The cavities are surrounded by areas of ground-glass opacities and nodular infiltrates. The findings are suggestive of a necrotizing infectious process. The scan is performed without contrast, as evidenced by the uniform density of the mediastinal structures.

description.short_caption: Stained lung aspirate showing branching fungal hyphae.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stained preparation of lung aspirate. The stain highlights numerous branching fungal hyphae, which are septate and exhibit acute-angle branching. The background consists of amorphous material, likely necrotic tissue or cellular debris. The staining technique appears to be a fungal-specific stain, such as Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) or periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), which enhances fungal structures.

Case_02013/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Stain of culture growth from lung aspirate.

description.short_caption: Lactophenol cotton blue stain showing fungal structures from lung aspirate culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a lactophenol cotton blue stain of fungal elements obtained from a lung aspirate culture. The fungal structures exhibit characteristic spiked or spiny spherical shapes, consistent with conidia or sporangia of a fungal organism. The blue staining highlights the morphology of the fungal elements against a pale background, aiding in identification. The image is magnified to show detailed fungal structures.
visible_findings: spiked or spiny spherical fungal structures
